31 When the current in a wire is 5.0 A, the average drift speed of the conduction electrons in the wire
is 7.4 × 10–4
m s–1.
Which row gives a possible cross-sectional area and number of conduction electrons per unit
volume for this wire?
number of conduction
cross-sectional
electrons per unit
area / m2
volume / m–3
A
7.2 × 10–7
1.2 × 1028
B
7.2 × 10–7
5.9 × 1028
C
2.3 × 10–6
7.3 × 1026
D
2.3 × 10–6
3.7 × 1027

hints: Notice the given current $5.0 \text{ A}$ and drift speed $7.4 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m s}^{-1}$ must be linked to both $A$ and $n$ in the table.
Recall $I = nAvq$ for a metal wire, where $q = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ is the electron charge.
Rearrange to $nA = I/(vq)$ and check which row gives a product $n \times A$ near $4.2 \times 10^{22} \text{ m}^{-2}$.
walkthrough: Identify the data: $I = 5.0 \text{ A}$, $v = 7.4 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and electron charge $q = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$.
State the governing relation for drift speed: $I = nAvq$, where $A$ is cross-sectional area in $\text{m}^2$ and $n$ is number per unit volume in $\text{m}^{-3}$.
Rearrange for the combined quantity fixed by $I$ and $v$: $nA = I/(vq)$.
Calculate $n \times A$ for each row: row B gives $(7.2 \times 10^{-7})(5.9 \times 10^{28}) \approx 4.2 \times 10^{22} \text{ m}^{-2}$, while the other rows give values about 5 to 25 times too small.
Only the row matching the required product can give $5.0 \text{ A}$ at that drift speed. This is option B.

A.explanation: The product $nA$ is about $8.6 \times 10^{21} \text{ m}^{-2}$, which gives a current of only about $1.0 \text{ A}$ with the given $v$.

B.explanation: The product $nA$ is about $4.2 \times 10^{22} \text{ m}^{-2}$, which gives $I = nAvq \approx 5.0 \text{ A}$ with the given $v$.

C.explanation: The product $nA$ is about $1.7 \times 10^{21} \text{ m}^{-2}$, which gives a current much smaller than $5.0 \text{ A}$.

D.explanation: The product $nA$ is about $8.5 \times 10^{21} \text{ m}^{-2}$, which gives a current of only about $1.0 \text{ A}$ with the given $v$.
